page: Microsoft Azure M16-8ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the MS series, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Hardware cache allocations comprise 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 38 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial, totaling 438.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an exceptionally dense allocation of 54.69 GB per vCPU. The instance is bundled with 550 GB of local SSD storage and features no hardware graphics accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate that this configuration prioritizes massive memory capacity over raw computational speed. The CPU scores place it in the lower tiers for compute throughput, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 884.0 and a multi-core score of 3437.0, along with a PassMark CPU score of 6364.45. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 17.31 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 26.14 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows a write bandwidth of 31.17 GB/sec for large 256MB blocks, alongside 36.54 GB/sec for uncached read operations. Workload-specific evaluations measured 5.28 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 5.75 GB/sec.

The constrained vCPU allocation paired with a 438.0 GB memory footprint offers a distinct architectural tradeoff, primarily targeting software environments where licensing costs scale per core. While computationally heavy processing will be limited by the 8 vCPUs, operations requiring huge in-memory footprints function effectively. Microsoft Azure M16-8ms is suitable for large-scale caching servers, in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and analytics tasks that require extreme memory density without requiring high compute parallelism.

Driven by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8280M processor on the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 438.0 GB of RAM, yielding roughly 54.7 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 550 GB of local SSD storage and operates without dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show moderate memory write bandwidth of 31.17 GB/sec alongside conservative compute results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 3437.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6364.45. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for software platforms licensed per core that demand extensive memory allocations. Microsoft Azure M16-8ms is best matched to in-memory databases, large Redis caching layers, and enterprise memory-intensive workloads.
